title: AI Engineer – Computer Vision & Deep Learning
description: About the Role AIOTY Labs is looking for an enthusiastic AI Engineer specializing in computer vision and deep learning to develop AI-powered inspection, defect detection, object recognition, and industrial automation solutions. The candidate will work on real-world AI vision applications deployed in manufacturing and industrial environments. Key Responsibilities Develop, train, and optimize computer vision and deep learning models. Work on object detection, classification, segmentation, OCR, and anomaly detection. Build AI-powered visual inspection systems for industrial applications. Develop solutions using Python, OpenCV, PyTorch, and TensorFlow. Train and fine-tune models using industrial image datasets. Work with YOLO architectures and other computer vision frameworks. Integrate industrial cameras, USB cameras, IP cameras, and Raspberry Pi cameras. Familiarity with image segmentation and industrial defect detection. Experience with Flask, FastAPI, or REST APIs. Knowledge of Git and Docker. Exposure to edge AI devices and industrial cameras. Qualifications B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, ECE, or related fields. Freshers with practical AI/ML projects, GitHub portfolios, or internships in computer vision are encouraged to apply. Pay: ₹250,000.00 - ₹300,000.00 per year Work Location: In person

title: AI Engineer
description: Job ID 74192 Category Global Data Insight & Analytics Location Chennai, India Work Type On-site Your primary mission will be to design, build, and take to production Generative AI tools and Large Language Model (LLM) applications that assist our analytical modelers in their day-to-day work — AI co-pilots for code generation, automated model-documentation and validation generators, and monitoring agents. You will own these solutions end to end: from architecture and model selection through cloud deployment, evaluation, observability, cost efficiency, and secure operation at scale on Google Cloud Platform. Beyond individual delivery, you will raise the bar for the team — defining engineering standards, reviewing designs, mentoring engineers, and partnering with platform, security, and model risk stakeholders so that GenAI capability lands in production safely and stays reliable. GenAI Solution Architecture: Architect and build production-grade LLM-powered applications, multi-agent systems, and workflow automations that assist model validators and quantitative modelers (e.g., independent validation agents, code-generation agents, monitoring agents). Own the technical design end to end, including model selection, prompting and orchestration strategy, retrieval design, tool integration, and evaluation criteria. Agentic & Retrieval Systems: Design agent architectures with clear tool boundaries, guardrails, and fallback behaviour. Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines over internal data, including chunking strategy, embedding selection, index design, hybrid search, and grounding/citation quality. Define how agents are evaluated for correctness, hallucination, and safety before release. Cloud Platform & Deployment Architecture: Design and operate highly available, multi-service AI workloads on Google Cloud Platform. Take ownership of the cloud architecture for AI applications — compute and serving patterns (Cloud Run, GKE), networking (VPC, private service access, egress controls), identity (IAM service accounts, least privilege), secrets (Secret Manager), storage and data services (GCS, BigQuery), and managed AI services (Vertex AI, Vertex Vector Search). Make deliberate trade-offs on scalability, latency, resilience, and cost. AI-Ops & LLMOps at Scale: Establish and mature AI-Ops/LLMOps pipelines covering the full lifecycle of Generative AI tools: automated deployment, model and prompt versioning, artifact and evaluation tracking, regression testing of prompts and agents, and continuous monitoring for quality, drift, latency, token cost, and hallucination mitigation. Build the reusable platform components that let other engineers ship GenAI safely without rebuilding foundations. CI/CD & Infrastructure as Code: Own CI/CD and infrastructure automation for AI services using Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Cloud Build, Kubernetes manifests) and GitOps practices. Deliver reproducible, auditable, environment-parity deployments with automated testing, progressive rollout, and clean rollback paths. Containerization & Performance Engineering: Package and serve AI applications as containerized microservices (Docker/Kubernetes), tuning autoscaling, resource requests and limits, cold-start behaviour, concurrency, caching, and batch versus real-time serving patterns. Drive down inference cost and latency without compromising quality. Observability, Reliability & SRE: Instrument AI systems with structured logging, distributed tracing, metrics, alerting, and dashboards. Define SLIs/SLOs for AI services, run incident response and root-cause analysis, and design for graceful degradation when upstream model providers or quotas fail. Security, Governance & Model Risk: Ensure every AI solution meets Ford's data privacy, security, compliance, and model-risk standards. Implement guardrails for internal data usage, prompt-injection and data-leakage protection, PII handling, access control, and audit trails — and produce the documentation and evidence needed for governance and audit review. Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Provide technical direction across the AI engineering team: set coding, architecture, and evaluation standards; conduct design and code reviews; mentor engineers and modelers on GenAI engineering practice; and translate ambiguous business problems into scoped, sequenced technical roadmaps. Act as a trusted reviewer for peers and a bridge between analytics, platform, and risk stakeholders. User-Centric Collaboration: Partner closely with analytical modelers to understand their daily bottlenecks, data prep challenges, and coding workflows, and convert those pain points into measurable AI products. Define success metrics up front and validate impact after adoption. Skills & Knowledge LLM & GenAI Technologies: Strong hands-on experience with LLM orchestration and agent frameworks (e.g., Google ADK, MCP), prompt and context engineering, function/tool calling, and working with both commercial and open-source foundation models — including reasoning about model capability, context limits, latency, and cost. Cloud Platform (GCP): Strong hands-on experience designing and operating on Google Cloud Platform: Cloud Run, Cloud Build, GKE, GCS, BigQuery, Vertex AI, Vertex Vector Search, IAM, VPC networking, Secret Manager, and Artifact Registry. Comfortable contributing to cloud architecture decisions — service selection, networking topology, quota management, and cost optimization. AI-Ops / LLMOps: Working knowledge of tools and platforms for model deployment, prompt and model versioning, evaluation harnesses, tracing, and monitoring of LLM and GenAI outputs in production. Experience defining evaluation datasets, automated scoring, and quality gates for GenAI releases. DevOps, IaC & SRE Practices: Good proficiency in CI/CD tooling, GitOps, containerization (Docker), orchestration (Kubernetes), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), and cloud-native monitoring, logging, and alerting. Vector Databases & Retrieval: Experience with vector search and embedding technologies (e.g., Vertex Vector Search, sentence transformers) and the retrieval patterns that sit on top of them — hybrid search, re-ranking, and grounded generation. Software Engineering: Strong hands-on Python engineering (5+ years), building APIs (FastAPI, Flask) that serve AI models to end users, with good typing, testing, packaging, and code-review practice. Enough full-stack understanding to integrate front-end, back-end, and AI services reliably. Security & Compliance: Familiarity with cloud security practices, identity and access management, secrets management, network policies, and compliance requirements in regulated environments. Analytics Workflow Understanding: Familiarity with the workflows of data scientists and modelers (data wrangling, feature engineering, model validation) so you can build tools that fit how they work. Qualifications & Experience Education: Master's or Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Cloud Computing, or a related technical discipline. Overall Experience: 6–9 years of software engineering, AI/ML, or cloud engineering experience, with experience owning systems in production. GenAI Production Experience: Around 3 or more years of hands-on experience building and deploying LLMs and Generative AI applications in production, including experience taking a solution from concept into production and iterating on it with users. Cloud & Platform Engineering: Experience building and operating AI/ML workloads on a major cloud provider (GCP preferred), including CI/CD for AI, containerization (Docker/Kubernetes), infrastructure as code (Terraform, Cloud Build, GKE), and production observability. Seniority & Scope: Experience leading technical work: contributing to architecture, helping set engineering standards, reviewing designs, mentoring engineers, and working effectively across teams. Comfortable working with independence and navigating some ambiguity. Communication: Ability to explain technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders — modelers, risk and governance partners, and leadership — and to work with them to agree priorities. Good to Have: Exposure to the Banking, Financial Services, or Credit Analytics industries; familiarity with SAS to help build code-translation or modernization tools for modelers; experience with machine learning engineering and model serving frameworks; and any relevant cloud certification (e.g., Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect, Professional Machine Learning Engineer, or Professional DevOps Engineer).

title: Data Scientist
description: You are a hands-on Data Scientist with 5+ years of experience applying statistics, machine learning, and analytics to solve business problems. You are skilled at translating ambiguous questions into analytical approaches, exploring complex data, and communicating actionable findings. You understand data engineering concepts and can work with data pipelines and cloud platforms to prepare reliable datasets and support model deployment. You enjoy collaborating across disciplines and taking ownership from problem definition through measurement of business impact. Responsibilities Partner with business stakeholders to frame problems, define success metrics, and translate business needs into analytical and data science solutions. Perform exploratory data analysis, statistical analysis, hypothesis testing, and experimentation to identify patterns, drivers, and opportunities. Design, develop, evaluate, and refine machine learning and statistical models for use cases such as forecasting, classification, segmentation, and anomaly detection. Apply appropriate validation methods; assess model performance and limitations; and communicate uncertainty, assumptions, and trade-offs. Prepare, transform, and integrate structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data. Develop reusable features and analytical datasets using Python and SQL. Collaborate with data engineers to understand and improve data pipelines, data models, quality checks, lineage, and access patterns; contribute to pipeline development where needed. Partner with ML engineers and engineering teams to operationalize models, automate workflows, and monitor model performance and data drift. Use cloud data and analytics platforms such as BigQuery and related orchestration or processing tools to access and process data at scale. Create visualizations, dashboards, and narratives that translate analytical results into actionable recommendations for technical and business audiences. Apply reproducible development and MLOps practices, including version control, testing, documentation, and CI/CD, in collaboration with engineering teams. Follow data governance, privacy, security, and responsible AI practices throughout the analytics and model lifecycle. Explore and evaluate emerging analytical, machine learning, and generative AI techniques where they address business needs. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field. 5+ years of hands-on experience in data science, advanced analytics, applied statistics, or machine learning. Strong proficiency in Python and SQL for data extraction, preparation, analysis, modeling, and automation. Solid understanding of statistical inference, hypothesis testing, experimental design, and model validation. Experience developing and evaluating predictive or statistical models using libraries such as scikit-learn, statsmodels, pandas, NumPy, and SciPy, or equivalent tools. Working knowledge of data engineering concepts, including ETL/ELT, data pipelines, data modeling, data quality, and orchestration. Experience working with cloud data platforms or enterprise data ecosystems, such as Google Cloud and BigQuery, or equivalent technologies. Experience communicating insights using visualizations, dashboards, or presentations for business and technical stakeholders. Familiarity with Git, code reviews, documentation, testing, and agile delivery practices. Strong problem-solving, collaboration, and communication skills.

description: Dear candidate, Please find the JD for the AI Developer role below, let me know if you have any questions. Role Summary We are looking for an AI Developer to design, build, and run agentic AI systems: software agents that plan, call tools, use company data, and complete multi-step tasks with controlled human oversight. You will work with several model providers and model sizes, choosing and routing between them for quality, speed, cost, and data-handling needs, ensuring no single model or vendor becomes a point of failure. This is a hands-on engineering role. You will write production code, build evaluation harnesses, and take agents from prototype to a monitored, secure, and supportable service. Key Responsibilities Agent design and build • Design and build agents and multi-agent workflows that plan, use tools, keep state, and complete multi-step business tasks. • Choose the right pattern for each problem (single agent, workflow with fixed steps, supervisor and worker agents, human-in-the-loop approval) and explain the trade-offs. • Write and maintain prompts, system instructions, tool definitions, and structured output schemas as versioned code. • Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and memory components, including document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector or hybrid search, and citation of sources. Multi-model strategy and orchestration • Work with several model families and providers (for example Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini, and open-weight models such as Llama or Mistral) through hosted APIs, cloud platforms (AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, Google Vertex AI), and self-hosted inference. • Build a model abstraction and routing layer that selects models by task type, quality, latency, cost, context length, and data-residency rules, with fallbacks when a provider fails or rate-limits. • Benchmark models on our own tasks and data, record the results, and re-evaluate when new models or versions are released. • Manage cost and latency through caching, batching, prompt compression, smaller models for simple steps, and token budgets. Tools and integrations • Connect agents to enterprise systems through REST and SOAP APIs, databases, message queues, files, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or equivalent tool standards. • Design tools with clear contracts, least-privilege access, input validation, idempotency, and safe handling of errors and retries. • Build integrations for document processing, search, email and messaging, workflow engines, and line-of-business applications such as claims, policy, and finance systems. Evaluation and quality • Build evaluation suites with golden datasets, automated checks, model-graded and human review, and regression tests that run on every change to prompts, tools, or models. • Measure task success, accuracy, groundedness, tool-call correctness, latency, and cost, and report them to stakeholders. • Run red-team and adversarial tests, including prompt injection, data leakage, and tool misuse. Safety, security, and governance • Apply guardrails: input and output filtering, permission checks before actions, approval steps for high-impact actions, and audit logs of every agent decision and tool call. • Protect personal and health data (PII and PHI) through masking, access control, encryption, retention rules, and region-appropriate hosting, in line with applicable regulations (for example data-privacy law and sector rules such as IRDAI). • Document model choices, known limitations, and risks, and support internal AI governance and model risk reviews. Operations and collaboration • Deploy agents through CI/CD pipelines to cloud or container platforms, with tracing, monitoring, alerting, usage and cost dashboards, and incident runbooks. • Provide L2/L3 support for agent incidents and carry out root-cause analysis, including bad outputs, tool failures, and model regressions. • Work with business owners, product managers, security, data, and integration teams to scope use cases, define success metrics, and plan rollout. • Review code and designs, mentor developers new to LLM engineering, and keep technical documentation and an internal catalog of agents, tools, and approved models. Required Qualifications • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience). • 4+ years of software development experience, including 1+ year building LLM-based applications that reached production. • Strong Python (and/or TypeScript or Java) with clean, tested, maintainable code. • Hands-on experience building agents with tool or function calling, structured outputs, and multi-step workflows, using a framework (for example LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, CrewAI, or a vendor agent SDK) or custom orchestration. • Practical experience with at least two model providers or families, and an understanding of their differences in context length, tool-use behavior, cost, latency, and data-handling terms. • Experience with RAG: embeddings, vector or hybrid search, chunking strategies, and retrieval quality tuning. • Experience designing evaluations for LLM systems (test sets, automated and human review, regression checks). • Strong API and integration skills (REST, JSON, OAuth2, webhooks) and SQL. • Working knowledge of Git, CI/CD, containers (Docker), and at least one cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud). • Understanding of LLM security risks (prompt injection, data leakage, excessive agent permissions) and of handling sensitive data. Preferred Qualifications • Experience running open-weight models (for example with vLLM, Ollama, or managed endpoints) and knowledge of quantization, serving, and GPU cost trade-offs. • Experience with fine-tuning or adapting models (LoRA, preference tuning, distillation) and judging when it is worth doing instead of prompting or RAG. • Experience with model gateways and routing tools (for example LiteLLM, or cloud-native gateways) and with observability tools for LLM tracing (for example Langfuse, LangSmith, or OpenTelemetry-based tracing). • Experience with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), agent-to-agent protocols, and building shared tool servers. • Experience with document AI: OCR, extraction from forms and PDFs, speech-to-text, and multilingual content. • Background in insurance, healthcare, or financial services, including claims, policy, or customer-service workflows. • Knowledge of AI governance frameworks and regulation (for example the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, or local data-protection and sector rules). • Experience with event-driven systems (Kafka, RabbitMQ, or cloud queues), workflow engines, and Kubernetes. • Relevant certifications (cloud, AI or ML, or security). Core Competencies • Engineering rigor: testing, version control, and measuring before and after every change • Sound judgment about when an agent is the right solution, and when a simple workflow or rule is better • Structured problem-solving and strong debugging skills for non-deterministic systems • Clear communication with business and technical stakeholders, including plain-language explanation of risks and limits • Security and privacy mindset, with caution about the permissions and data an agent can reach • Curiosity and discipline in tracking fast-moving models and tools without chasing every release • Ownership from prototype through production support Interested candidates please share the updated resume along with below details Employee Name : Contact Number: Email ID : Exp in yrs. : Current CTC : Expected CTC : Current Organization : Notice Period in Days: Current Location : Preferred Location : Counter Offer: Yes/No If Yes : Counter Offer CTC: Serving Notice Period: LWD:
